SAST/DAST Security Scan Report — Sprint 42
Meridian Capital

Prepared for Enterprise Risk Steering and Engineering Leadership. This document summarizes the static (SAST via Semgrep) and dynamic (DAST via internal harness) application security scan activities completed during Sprint 42. All analysis was performed against non-production branches and environments. No exploitable conditions were identified during this period; all SAST observations are informational in nature and reflect code quality, convention adherence, and rule calibration outcomes. DAST coverage focused on authenticated and unauthenticated surface validation, latency benchmarking, and schema consistency checks. The following tables provide document control details, execution metadata for CI pipelines, and rule pack inventory utilized in the scans.

SAST/DAST Execution Detail and Cross-Check
During Sprint 42, dynamic scanning validated endpoint availability, response schema stability, and standard header presence across representative service surfaces. Traffic was generated in a controlled pre-production environment with fully synthetic data. Authentication contexts included service accounts and role-scoped user journeys. Combined with SAST outcomes, the scans indicate consistent adoption of Meridian coding conventions and operational readiness indicators, with no actionable items required. The sections below detail DAST coverage, change-review dispositions, and trend metrics across recent sprints.

DAST traffic confirmed stable endpoint behavior, response schemas, and standard operational headers. No remediation or exception workflows were initiated. The next sprint will extend GraphQL pack adoption and continue latency benchmarking across partner integration flows.

Version: 3.1

Prepared by: Release Engineering (RELENG)
Primary Stakeholders: Digital Banking (DB), Capital Markets Technology (CMT), Enterprise Platform Services (EPS), Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Information Risk Office (IRO)

Executive Summary
This runbook governs the production deployment of Release 2026.07-B for Meridian Capital’s Digital Banking portfolio. The objective is to promote approved application components to the Production environment within the authorized window, with minimal service interruption and measurable adherence to operational quality gates. The document captures applicable approvals, scope boundaries, coordination plans, pre-deployment readiness confirmations, and the metrics framework for post-deployment validation.

The deployment is designed as a standard, low-complexity change per Change Risk Model v2.4, with an expected total active change duration under 90 minutes. No customer-impacting downtime is anticipated. All customer-facing updates have been conducted through feature toggles validated in lower environments.

Release and Change Parameters

- Release Name: 2026.07-B
- Change Ticket: MRC-CHG-04873 (CAB Approved)
- CAB Session: CAB-3125 (2026-07-10 14:00 UTC)
- Deployment Window: 2026-07-23 00:30–02:00 UTC (Approved by OPS-SCHED-2207)

- Rollback Package: RLB-2026.06-E (pre-validated)
- Release Train: Q3 Cycle A
- Change Type: Standard, Pre-Authorized Template ST-DB-001

Change Content Summary
The release includes non-breaking service updates and housekeeping changes across Digital Banking services. Functionality changes remain behind inactive flags in production. Schema evolution steps are forward-compatible and confirmed reversible through migration plan MIG-DB-146, with dry runs passing in PreProd. No infrastructure topology changes are included. Monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds are updated to align with new log attributes.

documents.title: Artifact Signing and Attestation Policy
pages:
Artifact Signing and Attestation Policy
Meridian Capital – Technology Risk Management

Document Identification and Control
Document ID: MC-TRM-SP-ASA-001
Title: Artifact Signing and Attestation Policy
Classification: Internal Use Only
Version: 1.0.0
Effective Date: 2026-04-15T00:00:00Z
Next Scheduled Review: 2027-04-15T00:00:00Z
Policy Owner: Security Architecture & Engineering (SAE)
Control Owner: Cryptographic Services & PKI (CSPKI)
Author: DevSecOps Program Office (DSO)
Primary Repository: TRM Confluence Space (REF: CNF-TRM-7321)
Change Control: CAB CRQ-2026-04421 (Approved 2026-04-08T14:35:00Z)
Approval Record: CISO Approval Ticket SEC-APP-2026-1187 (2026-04-10T09:12:44Z), CTO Co-Sign CTO-REF-2026-031 (2026-04-11T17:02:06Z)
Audit Traceability: Audit Plan Reference IAA-PLN-2026-19; Control Mapping RCM-ASA-2026-05

1. Overview and Purpose
This policy establishes Meridian Capital’s enterprise-wide requirements for cryptographic signing and attestation of software artifacts to ensure integrity, authenticity, provenance, and accountability across the software supply chain. It defines the minimum controls and governance necessary for build outputs, infrastructure-as-code packages, container images, machine learning model bundles, and other deployable units to be trusted within Meridian Capital’s environments. The policy seeks to mitigate risks of artifact tampering, unauthorized distribution, ambiguous asset lineage, and inadequate traceability that may result in operational disruption, regulatory findings, or client impact.

The scope of this document encompasses the normative requirements for artifact signing and attestation, the delineation of responsibilities across platform and product teams, the compliance metrics used to assess control effectiveness, and the mechanisms for independent assurance. The policy aligns with Meridian Capital’s Technology Risk Management Framework (TRMF) and complements the Secure Software Development Standard (MC-TRM-SSD-002), the Vulnerability Management Standard (MC-TRM-VMS-004), and the CI/CD Governance Standard (MC-TRM-CICD-007). It also maps to external expectations expressed in NIST SSDF practices, the Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts (SLSA) objectives, and sectoral regulatory obligations for software change control and operational resilience.

2. Policy Intent and Principles
The intent of the policy is to require that all artifacts promoted beyond development environments possess verifiable cryptographic signatures and attestation records sufficient to establish an unbroken chain of custody from source to release. These controls are principle-based and emphasize determinism, transparency, and fail-safe gating within the software delivery process. Policy application is technology-agnostic with respect to build systems and packaging formats, provided the requisite properties of signer identity, tamper-evidence, and auditable provenance are preserved.

To prevent ambiguity in trust decisions, signer identities must be rooted in centrally governed trust anchors, and attestations must be generated by controlled automation under the oversight of corporate services. Attestation content must be materially complete to support regulatory inquiry and incident reconstruction without exposing sensitive implementation details unnecessarily. The principles of least privilege, segregation of duties, and non-repudiation guide the management of signing authorities and the evaluation of attestations at promotion and deployment gates.

3. Authority and Enforcement
This policy is issued under the authority of the Chief Information Security Officer and the Chief Technology Officer. Compliance is mandatory across all lines of business, technology domains, and subsidiaries operating under the Meridian Capital brand. Enforcement occurs through automated policy evaluations at CI/CD promotion points, registry admission controls, and runtime admission policies governed by centrally managed trust policies. Non-compliant artifacts are not eligible for promotion, distribution, or execution in controlled environments. The Technology Risk Management function monitors adherence through defined key performance indicators and reports status quarterly to the Technology Risk Committee.

4. Background and Drivers
Meridian Capital’s 2025–2026 Software Supply Chain Assurance Review (TRM-ASR-2026-04) identified the need for consolidated artifact assurance controls amid increasing heterogeneity in build pipelines and packaging formats. Findings noted duplication of local signing practices, inconsistent attestation schemas, and insufficient lineage capture for infrastructure templates. While no client-facing incidents were attributed to artifact integrity during the review period, internal audit observation IAA-OBS-2025-33 recommended centralized governance, uniform metrics, and a formal policy to define minimum viable attestation content. External drivers include industry guidance on software supply chain transparency and regulator expectations for audit-ready provenance of production changes (see Compliance Note REG-CN-2026-12).

5. Document Governance and Maintenance
This policy is maintained by the DevSecOps Program Office with technical stewardship by Cryptographic Services & PKI and Security Architecture & Engineering. A comprehensive review is conducted annually or upon material change to trust anchors, regulatory obligations, or enterprise build services. Proposed revisions are initiated via TRM Ticket TRM-POL-CHANGE with linkage to CAB request records and security architecture review notes. The authoritative version is maintained in the TRM Confluence Space; derivative copies are informational only. Revision history and prior approvals are preserved for a minimum of seven years consistent with records retention schedules (Records Policy REF: RIM-2024-09).

6. Related Documents and References
- Secure Software Development Standard (MC-TRM-SSD-002; REF CNF-TRM-SSD-002)
- CI/CD Governance Standard (MC-TRM-CICD-007; REF CNF-TRM-CICD-007)
- Key Management and Cryptography Standard (MC-TRM-KMS-003; REF CNF-TRM-KMS-003)
- Software Composition and SBOM Standard (MC-TRM-SBOM-006; REF CNF-TRM-SBOM-006)
- Records Management Policy (RIM-2024-09; REF CNF-RIM-2024-09)
- Audit Control Matrix for Artifact Assurance (RCM-ASA-2026-05)
Crosswalks to external frameworks and regulatory references are documented in the Control Mapping Appendix (RCM-ASA-2026-05-APP).

7. Effective Date and Transition Guidance
The policy is effective as of 2026-04-15T00:00:00Z following CAB approval CRQ-2026-04421. Program-level adoption milestones are tracked under Initiative Portfolio ID DSO-PORT-2026-08 with quarterly checkpoints. Internal readiness assessment DSO-READ-2026-12 completed on 2026-03-28T16:48:19Z indicates that enterprise services required to satisfy this policy are operational and available to product teams. This policy supersedes prior guidance contained in Advisory TRM-ADV-2025-21 and formalizes controls that had been operating under interim directives.

8. Scope and Applicability
This policy applies to all software and infrastructure artifacts that are created, modified, or distributed by Meridian Capital and are intended for deployment, promotion, or execution in any non-development environment, including test, staging, pre-production, production, and disaster recovery. Applicability spans:
- Build outputs such as compiled binaries, libraries, container images, and platform plug-ins.
- Infrastructure-as-code and platform configuration packages, including but not limited to templates, charts, and modules that effect changes to compute, network, storage, and security configurations.
- Data processing components such as scheduled jobs, ETL/ELT packages, and streaming topology bundles where deployment artifacts are versioned and promoted.
- Machine learning model artifacts and associated inference/runtime packages managed through sanctioned model registries.
- Third-party artifacts imported via approved registries, repositories, or vendor platforms where Meridian Capital exerts control over promotion into enterprise environments.

Artifacts generated exclusively for ephemeral developer experiments confined to isolated sandboxes without any pathway to enterprise environments fall within the conceptual remit of the policy but are considered non-promotable until compliant signatures and attestations are present. All shared environments, including enterprise-wide sandboxes and integration test spaces, are classified as controlled environments for the purposes of this policy.

9. Definitions and Terminology
For the purposes of this policy, the following definitions apply:
- Artifact: A discrete, versioned unit of deployable software or configuration produced by a build or packaging process and distributed via a repository or registry under enterprise governance.
- Signing: The application of a cryptographic signature to an artifact to establish authenticity and provide tamper-evidence, verifiable against a recognized trust anchor.
- Attestation: A structured, verifiable statement bound to an artifact that conveys provenance and contextual evidence regarding how, when, and by whom the artifact was produced, tested, and approved for promotion.
- Provenance: The set of data describing the origin of an artifact, including source repository identifiers, commit references, controlled build environment identifiers, and build workflow metadata.
- Trust Anchor: A centrally governed and auditable root of trust used to validate signer identities and signatures across the enterprise.
- Non-repudiation: Assurance that the entity that performed a signing action cannot plausibly deny responsibility due to the use of governed identities and controls.
- Freshness: The condition in which an attestation remains within policy-defined temporal bounds relative to the artifact’s promotion or deployment event.
These definitions support consistent interpretation across teams and are harmonized with Meridian Capital’s cryptography and software development standards.

10. Governance and Roles
The following governance structure is established to ensure effective operation, oversight, and assurance of artifact signing and attestation:
- Security Architecture & Engineering (SAE) serves as policy owner, defines control objectives, and approves trust anchor design. SAE maintains the reference architecture for artifact assurance services and validates architectural conformance through design reviews (ARC Review Queue: SEC-ARC-2026).
- Cryptographic Services & PKI (CSPKI) acts as control owner and service provider for enterprise signing and trust validation capabilities. CSPKI governs signer identity lifecycle, trust anchor configuration, and service health reporting (Service ID: SVR-CSPKI-09).
- Platform Engineering (PE) delivers and operates CI/CD platform integrations, registry admission controls, and deployment policy engines that enforce compliance. PE tracks adherence through platform telemetry (KPI Registry: PE-KPI-ASA).
- DevSecOps Program Office (DSO) coordinates cross-team adoption, manages communications, and reports progress to the Technology Risk Committee. DSO maintains the enterprise rollout plan and readiness assessments (Portfolio DSO-PORT-2026-08).
- Release & Reliability (R&R) ensures release pipelines implement mandatory promotion gates and monitors artifact promotion events for policy alignment. R&R maintains operational runbooks and on-call dynamics for assurance services (Ops Calendar: RNR-OPS-ASA).
- Technology Risk Management (TRM) provides second-line oversight, maintains control testing plans, and consolidates quarterly risk reporting. TRM schedules and executes design effectiveness and operating effectiveness tests (Test Plan TRM-TEST-ASA-2026).
- Internal Audit (IA) performs independent assurance per the annual audit plan and reviews adherence to retention and traceability requirements (Audit Casebook: IAA-PLN-2026-19).
- Lines of Business Engineering Teams are accountable for producing policy-compliant artifacts and ensuring that their delivery pipelines engage approved assurance services. Engineering teams must maintain accurate inventory mappings between services and artifacts in the Configuration Management Database (CMDB Ref: CMDB-CI-ASA).

11. Control Objectives
The policy defines the following control objectives as measurable outcomes:
- Integrity: All promotable artifacts bear a valid enterprise-recognized signature at the time of promotion, registry admission, and deployment decision.
- Authenticity and Accountability: Signer identities are uniquely attributable to controlled automation or authorized roles with clear ownership and audit trails.
- Provenance and Traceability: Attestations provide sufficient detail to reconstruct source-to-release lineage, including linkage to code review events, build workflows, and test evidence identifiers.
- Freshness and Relevance: Attestations remain within defined temporal thresholds relative to the promotion or deployment event to prevent stale or ambiguous assurance signals.
- Revocation and Response Readiness: Trust anchors and signer identities are managed to support prompt revocation and environment-wide policy updates with auditable change control.

12. Compliance Measurement and Reporting
Compliance is monitored through enterprise metrics aggregated by Platform Engineering and validated by TRM. Primary indicators include signing coverage rate for promotable artifacts, successful attestation verification rate at promotion gates, attestation freshness conformance, and time-to-remediate for non-compliant promotion attempts. Reporting is standardized via the Artifact Assurance Dashboard (DASH-ASA-2026), updated daily at 03:15Z with data sourced from CI/CD telemetry, registry admission logs, and policy decision records. Quarterly summaries are filed under TRM Report TRM-QBR-ASA-2026 with attachments enumerating control test results and remediation tracking (e.g., REM-ASA-2026-Q2-014). The Technology Risk Committee minutes (TRC-MIN-2026-06-27) record the acceptance of these metrics and any mandated improvement actions.

The above governance, scope, and objectives form the foundation for the mandatory requirements and operational expectations that follow in subsequent sections of this policy. All teams are expected to align delivery practices and service configurations with these tenets to ensure sustained and auditable artifact trust across Meridian Capital’s technology estate.

2. Scope and Applicability

This policy applies to all software and data artifacts produced, modified, or distributed within Meridian Capital computing environments, irrespective of hosting model or deployment tier. Artifacts in scope include, but are not limited to, compiled application binaries, container images, virtual machine images, shared libraries, mobile application packages, infrastructure-as-code modules, configuration bundles, database migration scripts, ETL/ELT jobs, machine learning feature stores and models, serverless function packages, and internal command-line tools. In-scope artifacts also encompass metadata outputs such as software bills of materials (SBOMs), provenance attestations, build manifests, and release notes generated by enterprise build and release pipelines. Where business units procure third-party software or managed services that deliver deployable artifacts into Meridian environments, this policy governs the intake, verification, and ongoing validation of supplier attestations and signatures to the extent technically feasible and contractually supported.

The policy is enterprise-wide and extends across Global Markets Technology, Wealth Management Platforms, Corporate Functions IT, Treasury Operations Systems, Quant Research Compute, and Shared Services. Both persistent and ephemeral environments are covered, including development, system integration testing (SIT), user acceptance testing (UAT), pre-production, production, high-performance compute (HPC) clusters, and disaster recovery sites. Artifacts intended for internal experimental use are in scope once transmitted, stored, or executed within Meridian networks or integrated platforms. This delineation is recorded in GRC ticket GRC-AR-22691 (opened 2026-01-19T11:42:07Z) and ratified in the Security Architecture Review Board (SARB) minutes SARB-2026-02-06-Item4.

Enterprise platform components subject to this policy include the Meridian Build Fabric (MBF), Meridian Artifact Repository (MAR), Enterprise Signing Service (ESS), and the Continuous Compliance Telemetry Lake (CCTL). These platforms operate under the custodianship of Cloud Platform Engineering (CPE) and Secure Build Services (SBS), with operational guardrails documented in Change Advisory Board entry eCAB-2026-03-14-078. Integration points with Secrets Governance and Key Management Services (KMS) are maintained by the Enterprise PKI and Cryptographic Services team, with responsibility boundaries tracked in Ops Catalog entry OPS-CAT-SEC-0172, last updated 2026-04-02T08:10:55Z.

This policy governs both origin-signed artifacts (produced within Meridian pipelines) and intake-signed artifacts (originating from third parties and validated upon ingestion). Intake workflows are coordinated with Vendor Risk Management (VRM) to establish supplier assertion formats and verification evidence (reference VRM-INTK-5941, 2026-02-23T16:28:11Z). When supplier ecosystems evolve (e.g., upstream signing format changes), the cross-functional Impact Assessment Forum (IAF) convenes to evaluate operational implications and evidence continuity; see IAF memo IAF-2026-Q1-M04.

The policy aligns to Meridian control families SEC-ASAP-01 through SEC-ASAP-10 under the Information Security Management System (ISMS). The alignment map is maintained by Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) and references industry frameworks including ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A controls relevant to secure development and change, NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF) sections on provenance and integrity, and FFIEC guidance regarding change governance for financial institutions. The traceability matrix SEC-TRC-0029 (rev 3.1, approved 2026-03-05T13:03:29Z) associates this policy’s provisions with SOX ITGCs related to program changes and access.

Systems that distribute or deploy artifacts—such as release orchestration tools, cluster schedulers, and platform-as-a-service components—are consumers of signatures and attestations and are therefore within the chain of accountability. Distribution platforms operated by Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) for Cloud Runtime Services must verify signatures and enforce attestation-based policy decisions as part of their standard gatekeeping functions, with outcomes recorded to CCTL for audit analytics. Monitoring and alerting functions run by Security Operations (SecOps) consume failure signals to initiate incident triage (see incident template SECOPS-IM-Template-17).

Inherited obligations apply to joint ventures, subsidiaries, and strategic partners where Meridian asserts operational control over the build and deployment systems. Transitional arrangements for acquired entities are tracked via Integration Program Office records, with baseline conformance milestones captured in IPO-ART-2218 through IPO-ART-2224. As of baseline assessment CR-MBF-18644 (2026-03-07T09:12:18Z), all core lines of business have onboarded to ESS for origin signing, with two special-purpose research clusters scheduled for attestation telemetry integration by 2026-08-31 per Program Plan PMO-SEC-PL-2026-07.

Where data classification influences artifact handling, the Data Governance Council (DGC) stipulates that signing and attestation status be included among movement controls for artifacts associated with Confidential and Restricted data flows. This interaction is documented under DGC resolution DGC-2026-01-22-R2. The Records Retention function classifies signature and attestation artifacts as “Security Control Records” under retention class RR-17, with handling requirements cross-referenced to the Corporate Records Retention Policy FIN-REC-07.

For clarity, this scope statement does not narrow obligations by technology stack, hosting choice, or vendor selection; rather, it defines a uniform control baseline that is applied consistently enterprise-wide. Any future updates to the scope require SARB review and eCAB approval with a corresponding GRC impact assessment, and must be recorded with complete lineage in the Policy Library System of Record (PL-SOR) under document key POL-SEC-ASAP-2026-v1.x.

3. Roles and Responsibilities

Policy execution is distributed across defined roles to ensure clear accountability and uninterrupted operations. The Artifact Owner is accountable for the completeness and accuracy of attestations that describe build provenance, dependencies, and control posture for each release. Artifact Owners are designated in the Enterprise CMDB (CI attribute sec.artifactOwner) and must be traceable to a named individual within the relevant delivery organization. Ownership mapping evidence is maintained in GRC case GRC-OWN-3347 (consolidated quarterly; latest consolidation 2026-04-10T10:47:02Z).

Secure Build Services (SBS) is the control owner for origin signing within enterprise-managed pipelines. SBS operates ESS and ensures its availability, performance, and adherence to enterprise change governance. SBS coordinates with Cloud Platform Engineering (CPE) to maintain the reliability of MBF and MAR. Service reliability targets and supporting metrics (availability, verification latency, signature throughput) are tracked via SLO register SLO-SBS-ESS-2026 and reported to the Technology Risk Committee monthly. Service incidents and changes are governed under standard tickets (e.g., INC-ESS-2026-03-219, CHG-ESS-2026-04-082) with post-implementation reviews stored in the Service Management system.

The Enterprise PKI and Cryptographic Services team is the custodial owner of trust anchors and trust policy configuration used by verification systems. This includes lifecycle management, governance attestation, and audit evidence for key material and associated policy artifacts. The team maintains alignment with enterprise cryptographic standards and coordinates recertification cycles documented in CRY-KEY-LCM-Plan-2026 (approved 2026-02-28T15:55:44Z). Timeliness metrics capture median and tail verification latency, mean time to remediate attestation gaps identified at release, and supplier intake lead times. Section 5 — Control Governance, Ownership, and Change Authority

Meridian Capital establishes centralized governance for artifact signing and attestation under the Office of the CISO, with delegated day-to-day ownership to Secure Build Services (SBS) and Identity & Key Management (IKM). Control authority is documented in the GRC system of record (RiskTrack) under control families AC-SIGN-01 (Artifact Signing), AC-ATTEST-02 (Build Attestation), and AC-VERIFY-03 (Verification Gatekeeping). The definitive mapping of services and repositories to these controls is maintained by Cloud Platform Engineering (CPE) through the Service Inventory Registry (SIR-Prod), refreshed nightly at 02:30 UTC. As of 2026-06-30T00:00:00Z, the accountable control owner for AC-SIGN-01 is the Director, SBS (owner ID: OWN-4821), and the responsible engineering managers are designated per portfolio in tickets MCSEC-2026-11234 and CPE-OPS-2026-5507.

Executive sponsorship is provided by the Deputy CISO for Platform Security, who chairs the monthly Control Health Review (CHR) spanning SBS, IKM, CPE, Risk & Controls (R&C), Internal Audit, and Enterprise Architecture. Quorum is required (minimum four distinct director-level participants), and meeting minutes, attendance, and action items are filed under the collaboration workspace folder Ref: CHR/Signing/2026 with immutable hash anchors recorded in the Document Integrity Ledger (DIL). The CHR agenda consistently includes: control coverage metrics by service tier; change calendar review; nonconformance analysis; attestations lifecycle KPIs; and open risks with target remediation dates. CHR-2026-06 (held 2026-06-18T14:00:00Z) closed three action items: (1) updating the Tier 2 service onboarding checklist to reflect revised attestation schema v1.3 (SBS-ENG-2026-2099), (2) confirming completion of key rotation attestations for EU-region build pools (IKM-2026-4411), and (3) adding verification gate telemetry to the Control Health Dashboard (CPE-OBS-2026-771).

Change management for signing and attestation controls follows Enterprise RFC process (CAB-Standard), with SBS as the default change owner. Any material modification to signing infrastructure, attestation schemas, verification policies, or gate enforcement thresholds must be introduced via RFC with documented rollback, dependency mapping, and regression validation. Routine maintenance (e.g., non-breaking library updates, build runner patching) is executed under MMR (Minor Maintenance Release) tickets linked to a parent CAB record. For Q3 FY2026, RFC-CAB-2026-1817 covered the introduction of attestation schema v1.3 and verification engine enhancements; pilot validation was performed in non-production build pools BP-NP-07/08 between 2026-06-05T09:00:00Z and 2026-06-10T22:00:00Z, with success criteria met and sign-off captured from SBS, IKM, and CPE. No emergency changes are permitted for signing keys or policy definitions; where urgent mitigations are required, deployments are deferred or blocked until a standard CAB-approved change is completed.

Ownership boundaries are explicit and enforce separation of duties. SBS operates the signing and attestation services and maintains the verification gate in the CI/CD control plane. IKM manages key material lifecycle, including provisioning, rotation, and archival in FIPS-validated modules, and enforces administrative access controls. CPE ensures integration of policy gates across deployment orchestrators and maintains telemetry exports to the enterprise observability stack. R&C performs quarterly control testing and assures alignment with regulatory control frameworks (e.g., SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001 control mappings as documented in R&C-MAP-2026-07). Internal Audit independently evaluates control design and effectiveness at least annually; the most recent audit cycle (IA-2026-014) recorded effective ratings for design and operating effectiveness with follow-up recommendations limited to documentation clarity for service-specific onboarding checklists.

Escalations follow a 24x7 model. Control degradations detected by health monitors initiate incident tickets in the Operational Risk queue (OPRISK) and page the SBS on-call via the Enterprise Pager roster (rotation SBS-OC-PRD, weekly handoffs Monday 08:00 local). Example: OPRISK-2026-3019 was raised at 2026-05-27T03:11:42Z for elevated attestation retrieval latencies exceeding the defined threshold in the EU-West region; the issue was triaged and resolved within the target service level with no policy downgrades or gate bypasses. If any degradation could lead to unsigned or unverified artifacts progressing, the gates default to block and a business-impact assessment is performed by the affected service owners alongside SBS and R&C. Deviations are not authorized; remediation is required prior to progression. Status communications follow the standard incident communications protocol and are archived in the incident repository with cross-links to supporting telemetry captures.

No ad hoc overrides are permitted. Temporary accommodations such as manual attestations, key substitutions, or selective disabling of verification rules are prohibited. Where development timelines require earlier integration, project plans must reflect onboarding to the control framework as an entry criterion. The “Ready for Build Promotion” milestone in the Enterprise Delivery Framework (EDF) explicitly includes verification of signing and attestation readiness; gating is enforced by the CI/CD control plane. The Dev Enablement team maintains adoption guides and FAQs on the Developer Portal (Doc IDs DEV-SEC-SIGN-101 through -110) and tracks onboarding via the Product Security Readiness Kanban (PSRK). As of 2026-06-30, 97% of active product teams have fully integrated the verification gate at all required stages; remaining teams (tracked in PSRK-2026-Backlog items 55, 72, and 81) have committed remediation plans with dates approved by their respective VPs of Engineering.

Risk acceptance is out of scope for this control; if a service cannot meet requirements, deployment is halted and remediation plans are executed. R&C maintains a watchlist of services approaching control deadlines and coordinates with Portfolio Risk Managers to ensure delivery plans include necessary technical work. Where architectural constraints are material, the Architecture Review Board (ARB) must be engaged to align service design to policy rather than requesting policy exceptions. All decisions, minutes, and supporting documents are retained under the DIL anchor scheme to preserve auditability and chain of custody.

Section 6 — Monitoring, Metrics, Reporting, and Audit Readiness

Control health is continuously assessed through telemetry captured at signing, attestation publication, and verification points. The Control Health Dashboard (CHD), maintained by CPE Observability, aggregates indicators including: proportion of artifacts signed per release train; attestation generation success rates; verification gate pass/fail counts; median and p95 attestation retrieval latency; and attestation schema compliance. Data sources are normalized into the Enterprise Metrics Bus (EMB) with entity keys aligned to SIR-Prod service identifiers. As of the June 2026 reporting cycle (report REF: CHD-2026-06, generated 2026-06-29T23:50:00Z), Tier 0/1 services achieved 100% signed artifacts with 100% retrievable attestations, and Tier 2/3 services averaged 99.6% signed artifacts with 99.4% retrievable attestations. Attestation retrieval p95 latency remained within target, measured at 410ms in NA-East, 460ms in EU-West, and 505ms in AP-Southeast.

Key performance indicators and thresholds are defined and reviewed quarterly:
- Signature Coverage: 100% for Tier 0/1, ≥99.5% for Tier 2/3. Measured at release completion and post-deployment verification.
- Attestation Availability: ≥99.9% within 60 seconds of artifact indexing for Tier 0/1, and within 120 seconds for Tier 2/3.
- Verification Gate Efficacy: False-negative rate of zero, false-positive rate ≤0.05% of gate decisions per month.
- Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) Attestation Mismatch: ≤5 minutes from publication to detection.
- Mean Time to Restore (MTTR) Control Degradation: ≤4 hours for Tier 0/1 impacting events; ≤8 hours for Tier 2/3.

Performance against these thresholds is summarized in the monthly Control Performance Report (CPR). CPR-2026-06 recorded no Tier 0/1 threshold breaches. Two Tier 2/3 services missed the attestation availability objective for a single release window due to dependent storage replication delays; both were contained by gate blocks, with remediation tracked in SBS-ENG-2026-2231 and CPE-OPS-2026-5793. No artifacts advanced without successful verification, and post-incident reviews confirmed monitoring sensitivity and alert routing functioned as designed.

Evidence generation for audit readiness is automated. For each release, a Release Evidence Package (REP) is compiled, containing: artifact manifest with checksums; signing event metadata (timestamp, signer service ID, key reference alias); attestation document references with integrity hashes; verification gate result logs; and control oversight approvals where applicable (e.g., CHR acknowledgment for schema migrations). REPs are stored in the Evidence Vault with seven-year retention, WORM protection enabled, and DIL anchors to support non-repudiation. Internal Audit has read-only access to REPs via the Audit Portal, with search parameters scoped by service, time window, and control ID. During IA-2026-014 sampling, auditors retrieved REPs for 25 releases across three regions without assistance and validated completeness against the audit program steps (AUD-PGM-2026-014-S8).

Continuous control testing (CCT) is performed by R&C and SBS. Synthetic validation jobs run hourly across representative pipelines to confirm: signing invocation occurs; attestations are generated using the current approved schema; and verification gates block on expected failure modes. Results are logged under the CCT dataset with pass/fail and latency histograms. June 2026 CCT stats showed 99.98% pass rate across 2,160 runs; three failures in AP-Southeast were linked to a transient dependency timeout, already addressed in CPE-OBS-2026-812. Quarterly, R&C executes design-effectiveness walk-throughs and operating-effectiveness re-performance of controls, with outputs documented in RNC-TEST-2026-Q2. Findings for Q2 included a recommendation to enhance the homepage of the CHD with contextual explanations for threshold changes; SBS applied the improvement under DEV-PORTAL-2026-141 by 2026-06-25T18:22:07Z.

Reporting obligations include consolidated summaries to the Technology Risk Committee (TRC). The TRC briefing pack (TRC-BR-2026-07) includes a one-page dashboard view, material incidents since the prior meeting, adoption trajectory by service tier, and a preview of upcoming change windows with risk commentary. The July pack highlights completion of schema v1.3 rollout, stabilization of retrieval latency in APAC regions, and an ongoing initiative to standardize attestation producers across legacy build pools. Risk statements are aligned to the enterprise risk taxonomy, with inherent and residual ratings validated by Portfolio Risk Managers.

Training and access oversight underpin measurement reliability. SBS and IKM engineers with administrative responsibilities complete annual control-specific training (LMS course SEC-PLT-204) and quarterly reviews of privileged access (IKM-AAR-2026-Q2). Access reviews conducted 2026-06-12T10:00:00Z confirmed least-privilege for all named administrators and removal of two stale service accounts (IAM-OPS-2026-332). Changes to monitoring thresholds or report definitions require dual approval from SBS and R&C, logged in change tickets and recorded in the CHD changelog (CHD-CHNG-LOG entries 2026-06-07#14 and 2026-06-21#03).

Disaster recovery and continuity targets for monitoring and evidence systems are defined to maintain auditability. The CHD and Evidence Vault maintain regional redundancy with documented RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 15 minutes. DR exercises executed 2026-05-14T02:00:00Z (exercise ID DR-CHD-2026-05) demonstrated recovery within targets, with after-action items limited to dashboard cache warming optimization (CPE-OBS-2026-799). Quarterly, SBS validates that DIL anchors reconcile after failover and that evidence record integrity remains intact, with reconciliations documented in SBS-CTRL-REC-2026-Q2.

Third-party and open-source dependencies are included in metrics and reporting through supplier attestations and SBOM ingestion. Supplier attestations are validated at intake and linked to internal REPs, with verification outcomes visible in CHD. Where supplier attestations are delayed or incomplete, gates retain default-block posture until artifacts are fully verified. Supplier Management tracks these events in SUP-MGMT-2026-119; June metrics indicate 100% compliance among strategic suppliers and 98.7% among long-tail vendors, with remediation plans active for the remainder.

Collectively, these monitoring, metrics, and reporting practices ensure the Artifact Signing and Attestation Policy is measurable, transparent, and auditable, and that deviations are promptly detected, contained by default controls, and remediated within defined service levels.

2. Instrumentation and Event Taxonomy
The attestation verification service (internal service code: Aegis-Verify) and the signing service (internal service code: Aegis-Sign) emit normalized, structured events with the following canonical categories:

- SEC-LOG-ATT-ISSUE: Attestation issuance events with provenance references, build context identifiers, and policy mappings.
- SEC-LOG-SIGN-KEY-USE: Key usage telemetry, including non-sensitive key IDs, rotation epochs, and mTLS client identity references.
- SEC-LOG-POLICY-EVAL: Policy engine rule set evaluations and decision traces (hash-linked to rule set version).
- SEC-LOG-REGISTRY-GATE: Deployment registry admission and deny events at promotion boundaries (dev->test->prod) with associated artifact metadata.

All events are stamped in UTC and include consistent field names aligned to the SSCS Observability Contract v2.8 (schema ID: MC-SSCS-OBC-2_8), effective 2026-03-31. The schema is subject to change control via JIRA epic SEC-OPS-PLAT-432, with CAB approval required for field additions or phase-outs to avoid downstream analytic breaks.

Meridian Capital’s Artifact Signing and Attestation Policy is mapped to the enterprise control framework and aligned with external standards where applicable. The authoritative control mappings are maintained in the GRC platform (record set: GRC-SSCS-CTRL-SET-11, last updated 2026-06-12T10:49:58Z, Information Risk Management). Key internal controls include:
- MC-SSCS-01: All production-bound artifacts must carry a valid, policy-conformant attestation verified at promotion time.
- MC-SSCS-02: Signing and verification services must enforce strong, centrally managed identities and record non-sensitive key usage telemetry.
- MC-SSCS-03: Attestation and signing events must be logged with integrity-protected, time-synchronized records and retained per policy.
- MC-SSCS-04: Changes to signing, verification, and policy engines must follow CAB governance with documented testing and rollback plans.
- MC-SSCS-05: Quarterly reviews must assess attestation coverage, provenance completeness, and adherence to segregation-of-duties principles.

Evidence artifacts supporting these controls are curated in the “SSCS Evidence Locker” within the GRC repository (folder ID: EV-SSCS-2026-Q2). Artifacts include signed dashboard exports, attestation policy manifests (hash-referenced), CAB approvals, and sampling trace packages for selected applications. Evidence index entries contain immutable hashes and retention tags linked to case IDs for traceability.

12. Monitoring, Measurement, and Continuous Assurance

Meridian Capital maintains a continuous assurance program to validate that artifact signing and attestation activities perform reliably, at scale, and in conformance with policy intent. The objective is to deliver measurable confidence that every promotable build artifact is signed by an approved organizational key, attested with verifiable provenance and supply chain metadata, and verified at enforcement gates prior to deployment. This section defines the monitoring framework, the key performance indicators (KPIs) used for management oversight, the reporting cadence, and the feedback mechanisms by which the enterprise iteratively improves the control environment.

12.1 Control Objectives and KPIs

Control objectives for the Artifact Signing and Attestation Policy are expressed as service and conformance targets that can be continuously observed and trended. The current KPI set, owned jointly by DevSecOps Engineering and Platform Assurance, is as follows:

- Signing Coverage: Percentage of release-eligible artifacts that carry a valid organizational signature at the time of promotion decision. Target: 99.5%, minimum acceptable: 99.0%.
- Attestation Completeness: Percentage of promotion decisions accompanied by a verifiable attestation bundle including provenance, build recipe references, and policy evaluation verdict. Target: 99.5%, minimum acceptable: 99.0%.
- Verification Gate Efficacy: Percentage of enforcement gate decisions that correctly accept compliant artifacts and reject non-compliant artifacts without manual rework. Target: 99.9%, minimum acceptable: 99.7%.
- Control Latency: Median and 95th percentile time from artifact availability to signed and attested status, measured per pipeline tier. Target: median ≤ 120 seconds; P95 ≤ 300 seconds.
- Rotation Timeliness: Completion of planned key rotation tasks within the approved change window. Target: 100%.
- Evidence Integrity: Percentage of required evidence elements (signature references, attestation digests, gate decision logs) written to the immutable evidence store within 15 minutes of event occurrence. Target: 99.9%.

12.2 Data Sources and Telemetry

Monitoring is derived from corroborated signals emitted by the CI/CD controllers, the signing service orchestration layer, the key management control plane, the attestation repository, and the enterprise logging platform. Telemetry is standardized to a normalized event schema that includes artifact digest, signature subject, attestation identifier, build pipeline identifier, and decision outcome. Cross-system correlation is performed using a deterministic artifact correlation key. All timestamps are recorded in UTC with synchronized clock sources. Platform Assurance validates ingestion completeness daily by reconciling aggregate counts for “build finalized,” “signature created,” “attestation published,” and “gate verified” events.

13. Audit Readiness, Records Management, and Attestation Evidence

Meridian Capital structures artifact signing and attestation controls to be audit-ready at all times. Evidence is produced contemporaneously, retained according to the enterprise records schedule, and organized for efficient retrieval to support internal audit procedures, regulatory examinations, and customer due diligence. This section codifies the evidence catalog, retention requirements, access governance, compliance mappings, and independent assessment practices that sustain continuous audit readiness for the policy domain.

13.1 Evidence Catalog and Retention

The evidence catalog defines the authoritative record for each control assertion. At minimum, the following are maintained:

- Signature Evidence: immutable references to signature metadata, including artifact digest, signer identity, signature timestamp, and verification outcome recorded at enforcement. Stored in the enterprise evidence repository with a seven-year retention.
- Attestation Evidence: provenance statements, build configuration identifiers, policy evaluation results, and attestations of control conformance captured at build completion and re-validated at promotion. Retained for seven years.
- Decision Logs: enforcement gate decisions, including acceptance or rejection rationale and policy version in effect. Retained for seven years.
- Operational Telemetry: service health metrics, alert acknowledgments, and maintenance records relevant to signing and attestation service reliability. Retained for three years.
- Governance Records: approvals, meeting minutes, KPI packs, and change advisories that authorize policy and platform changes. Retained per Corporate Records Management schedule (minimum seven years).

Evidence is written to an append-only storage class with integrity protections, including cryptographic hashing and periodic ledger reconciliation, and is replicated across fault domains for durability. Records subject to legal hold are marked immutable pending disposition guidance from the Office of the General Counsel (ref. LEG-HOLD-2026-044). The Evidence Steward within Platform Assurance is the accountable owner for catalog integrity, with daily completeness checks and monthly reconciliation reported under EVID-RECON-2026 series tickets.

13.2 Access Governance and Segregation of Duties

Access to evidence and signing operations is restricted to defined roles, each assigned on the principle of least privilege with documented approvals through Identity Governance workflows. The following functional roles are in force: Key Custodian (custodial oversight of key lifecycle operations), Signing Service Operator (service reliability and configuration management), Release Approver (promotion decision authority), and Evidence Auditor (read-only access to evidence repositories). No individual may hold conflicting roles that would enable initiation and approval of the same promotion decision. Temporary elevated access is time-bound and subject to supervisory approval, with automated expiration and post-facto review logged under ACCESS-REVIEW-2026 monthly cycles. As of 2026-06-30, all quarterly access certifications for these roles are complete (IGA-CERT-2026-Q2 closed 2026-07-03T09:21:44Z) with zero exceptions noted.

13.3 Compliance Mappings

The policy and its control set map to Meridian Capital’s enterprise control framework and external standards relevant to secure software lifecycle governance. Mappings are curated by Technology Controls Oversight and maintained in the Controls Library (CTL-LIB-SS-ATTEST-v2.3). Representative alignments include lifecycle controls for change management, cryptographic control management, integrity verification, and records retention. These mappings facilitate audit scoping, test planning, and external reporting, and are reviewed semi-annually or upon material control changes.

13.4 Responding to External Requests

11. Monitoring, Measurement, and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Meridian Capital maintains a structured measurement framework to ensure the efficacy, consistency, and timely operation of artifact signing and attestation across all approved build and release pathways. Monitoring focuses on both control effectiveness (e.g., signing occurrence and verification success) and operational health (e.g., job queue latency, attestation issuance throughput). Metrics are curated by the Supply Chain Telemetry Service (SCTS) operated by DevSecOps Engineering (DSE) and continuously reconciled with the Enterprise Key Management Service (EKMS) audit stream and the Release Governance Ledger (RGL) operated by the Software Supply Chain PMO. Each metric is versioned and cataloged with a unique identifier for traceability, and is reviewed in accordance with the Governance Cadence described in Section 13.

The following KPIs are considered control-critical and are tracked at the application, business unit, and enterprise levels:
- Metric ASM-01: Artifact Signing Coverage. Definition: proportion of releasable artifacts that carry a current, policy-aligned digital signature from an approved trust root. Service Level Objective (SLO): ≥ 99.5% monthly. Rolling 90-day baseline (as of 2026-06-30T23:59:59Z): 99.72%. Measurement Notes: derived from repository event hooks, pipeline manifests, and signature verification receipts; reconciled against permitted artifact types enumerated in Control ASC-07.
- Metric ASM-02: Verification Success Rate. Definition: proportion of signature verifications completed successfully in pre-deploy gates. SLO: ≥ 99.9% monthly. Rolling 90-day baseline: 99.93%. Measurement Notes: event stream emitted by Gatekeeper-Verify jobs in all CI/CD systems and correlated to Release Ticket IDs.
- Metric ASM-03: Attestation Freshness. Definition: median age (in hours) of attestation documents (SLSA provenance, SBOM attestations) at the time of release promotion. Target: ≤ 24 hours median; ≤ 72 hours 95th percentile. Rolling 90-day baseline: 13.4 hours median; 39.7 hours p95.
- Metric ASM-04: Trust Root Alignment. Definition: percentage of signatures anchored to active, approved roots per EKMS Trust Policy TRP-04. SLO: 100%. Rolling 90-day baseline: 100%. Measurement Notes: validated via EKMS Trust Graph version 2026.6.
- Metric ASM-05: Key Lifecycle Compliance. Definition: percentage of signing keys meeting rotation and usage constraints (Control KLC-02). Target: 100%. Rolling 90-day baseline: 100%. Measurement Notes: computed from EKMS key usage logs and CRL deltas.
- Metric ASM-06: Gate Bypass Incidents. Definition: count of release candidates requiring manual governance intervention to reconcile signing or attestation signals. Threshold: 0 per month. Rolling 90-day baseline: 0. Measurement Notes: controlled via Change Tickets; see CHG-2026-05-1419 and CHG-2026-06-0908 for routine gate configuration changes.

SCTS processes and stores metrics on a near-real-time basis (sub-5-minute end-to-end latency target), with canonicalization performed once daily at 02:15:00Z. Dashboards are published to the enterprise observability portal with data sources declared and signed by the telemetry pipeline to prevent tampering. All KPI definitions carry a stewardship assignment; as of 2026-07-01T12:00:00Z, ASM-01 through ASM-06 are stewarded by DSE with Risk, Controls & Compliance (RCC) oversight. Material deviations from SLOs generate alerts in the Security Operations Center (SOC) under event class SCT-ALRT, with escalation paths documented in RCC Playbook RC-PB-19. During Q2 2026, three advisory alerts were generated (TKT: DSE-ALRT-2026-05-1127, DSE-ALRT-2026-06-0203, and DSE-ALRT-2026-06-2711), all closed as non-conformity-avoided events following telemetry tuning; no policy non-conformities were recorded.

12. Auditability, Evidence, and Retention
The policy requires that evidence demonstrating compliant artifact signing and attestation be complete, durable, and independently verifiable. Evidence artifacts include: (a) signed verification receipts for each build and promotion gate; (b) attestation bundles comprising provenance statements and SBOM attestations linked to immutable artifact digests; (c) EKMS key lifecycle logs (creation, use, rotation, and revocation events); and (d) change and approval metadata from the Release Governance Ledger. For each release candidate, the RGL maintains a cryptographic linkset that binds artifact digests, signature envelopes, and attestation identifiers, enabling later reconstruction during audits and investigations.

Evidence must be retained for a minimum of seven (7) years following the last distribution of the associated artifact or for the period prescribed by regulatory retention schedules applicable to the business unit, whichever is longer. Storage must be Write Once Read Many (WORM) compliant and replicated across at least two independent regions under Meridian Capital’s standard business continuity tier for regulatory records (BCT-2). The Records & Archives team (R&A) certifies the immutability controls quarterly; attestations for Q2 2026 were completed and recorded under RAA-2026-06-30-IMM, with no deviations. Access to evidence is governed by role-based access control (RBAC) integrated with Identity Governance & Administration (IGA); access requests and approvals are logged and subject to monthly RCC sampling.

Internal Audit may request on-demand evidence packages for scoped reviews. During the Internal Audit thematic review of software supply chain controls (AUD-2026-05-SSCX), the audit team requested and received 45 evidence packages covering April–May 2026 releases across four business units. All packages were delivered within the agreed SLA (5 business days). Two minor documentation completeness findings (AUD-2026-05-SSCX-F12 and F19) were remediated by enhancing receipt bundling in SCTS v2026.6.4 (CHG-2026-06-1205) and updating the RGL export manifest template (RFC-2026-06-1217). No control design or operating effectiveness issues were identified.

18. Glossary and Acronyms
- Artifact: A discrete, versioned output of a build process (e.g., package, container image) that is promoted through release stages and subject to signing and attestation.
- Attestation: A cryptographically verifiable statement asserting properties of an artifact (e.g., provenance, build environment, SBOM) linked to the artifact’s immutable identifier.
- Attestation Freshness: The temporal delta between the creation of an attestation and the promotion of the associated artifact.
- EKMS: Enterprise Key Management Service responsible for the lifecycle of cryptographic keys and trust policy enforcement.
- Provenance: Evidence describing how an artifact was produced, including source references and build parameters, captured in a standardized format.
- Release Governance Ledger (RGL): The authoritative record of approvals, signatures, attestations, and promotion decisions for releasable artifacts.
- Root of Trust (Trust Root): A cryptographic anchor approved by Meridian Capital and governed by EKMS Trust Policy.
- SCTS: Supply Chain Telemetry Service that aggregates, normalizes, and signs control telemetry for dashboards and audits.
- SLO: Service Level Objective indicating the target performance threshold for a metric.
- WORM: Write Once Read Many storage capability used for records immutability.
